```{r setup}
#| include: false
source("theme.R")
library(housepi)
set.seed(42)
```

In this vignette we present all available options for the choice of the prior and Monte Carlo rule in `housepi`. 

# Continuous Priors

To perform the sampling we consider the "blank" model, i. e. a data independent template model, with loglikelihood always equal to zero.
Here's the full list of available continuos distributions present in `housepi`:
```{r}
# real distributions in housepi
continuos_distri <- c("unif", "norm", "lnorm", "gamma",
                      "weibull", "rayleigh", "beta", "exp")

# generate list with definitions
defs <- Map(list, prior = continuos_distri) |>
  setNames(continuos_distri)

# create an instance of the blank model
new_housepi_model("blank") |>
  load_parameter_list(from = defs) |>
  # perform the sampling with the inference command
  infer() |>
  get_param_draws() |>
  bayesplot::mcmc_dens()
```

Here we associated definitions of parameters to infer with default arguments and default proposer rules (Gibbs sampling). 

## Provide a Custom Range

We then test various example MISSING

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(ggplot2)

new_housepi_model("blank") |>
  load_parameter_list(
    default = list(prior = "norm"),
    below = list(prior = "norm", min = -1),
    above = list(prior = "norm", max = 1),
    both = list(prior = "norm", min = -1, max = 1)
  ) |>
  infer() |>
  get_param_draws() |>
  bayesplot::mcmc_dens() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-3, 3), ylim = c(0, 0.6)) +
  geom_vline(
    data = data.frame(
      Parameter = c("below", "above", "both", "both"),
      xintercept = c(-1, 1, -1, 1)
    ),
    aes(xintercept = xintercept),
    colour = "coral", linewidth = 1, linetype = 2
  )
```

# Discrete Priors

```{r}
#| include: false
bayesplot::color_scheme_set(scheme = "orange")
```

Here's the full list of available discrete distributions present in `housepi`:

```{r}
# discrete distributions in housepi
discrete_distri <- c("pois", "binom", "nbinom", "geom")
defs <- Map(list, prior = discrete_distri) |>
  setNames(discrete_distri)

new_housepi_model("blank") |>
  load_parameter_list(from = defs) |>
  infer() |>
  get_param_draws() |>
  bayesplot::mcmc_hist(binwidth = 1)
```

## How to Discretize Continuos Priors

Previous continuous priors can be chosen to be discretized simply by adding the flag `discr = TRUE`.

```{r}
reduc_distri <- continuos_distri[continuos_distri != "beta"]
defs <- Map(list, prior = reduc_distri, discr = TRUE) |>
  setNames(reduc_distri)

new_housepi_model("blank") |>
  load_parameter_list(from = defs) |>
  infer() |>
  get_param_draws() |>
  bayesplot::mcmc_hist(binwidth = 1)
```

# MCMC Proposer Rules

```{r}
#| include: false
bayesplot::color_scheme_set(scheme = "brightblue")
```

```{r}
# available proposer rules in housepi
proposer_rules <- c("sample", "unif", "norm", "lnorm")
defs <- Map(list, prior = "norm", min = 0,
            rule = proposer_rules, scale = 0.01) |>
  setNames(paste("rule", proposer_rules))

new_housepi_model("blank") |>
  load_parameter_list(from = defs) |>
  infer(n_steps = 100) |>
  get_param_draws() |>
  bayesplot::mcmc_trace()
```
Note that the proposer rule "lnorm" does not fit the case of negative values.

## Role of Finite Adaptation

```{r}
new_housepi_model("blank") |>
  load_parameter_list(from = defs) |>
  infer(n_steps = 100, n_adapt = 1000) |>
  get_param_draws() |>
  bayesplot::mcmc_trace()
```
